result.markdown: --- title: "Navigating the Decision Tree" subtitle: "Choosing the Right Visualization for Your Data" author: "Sparrow" date: "2026-11-20" format: revealjs: theme: serif slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true code-fold: true chalkboard: true preview-links: true center: true zoom: true fig-align: center footer: "Data Visualization Decision Framework" transition: fade transition-speed: default --- # Navigating the Decision Tree {.title-slide} ## Choosing the Right Visualization for Your Data **A Practical Framework Based on Analytical Goals** --- # The 3-Step Framework ## Your Roadmap for Visualization Selection ::: {.incremental} 1. **Identify Your Data Type** - What kind of data do you have? (Numeric, Categorical, Temporal, etc.) 2. **Define Your Analytical Goal** - What do you want to communicate? (Compare, Distribute, Show Relationships, etc.) 3. **Select the Appropriate Chart** - What visualization best achieves your goal? ::: --- # The Seven Analytical Goals ## Color-Coded Framework | Goal | Symbol | Question | Purpose | |------|--------|----------|---------| | **Distribution** | ● | "What's the spread?" | Show data spread, shape, outliers | | **Correlation** | ● | "How do things relate?" | Show relationships between variables | | **Ranking** | ● | "What's the order?" | Compare values in order | | **Part of Whole** | ● | "What's the composition?" | Show proportions/percentages | | **Evolution** | ● | "How does it change over time?" | Track trends and changes | | **Maps** | ● | "Where is it located?" | Geographic/spatial distribution | | **Flow** | ● | "How does it move?" | Movement, transitions, journeys | --- # Color Legend: Chart-to-Goal Mapping ## Quick Reference - What Each Color Means - **●** **Gold/Yellow = Distribution** - Shows data spread, frequency, shape, outliers - **●** **Blue = Correlation** - Shows relationships, associations between variables - **●** **Green = Ranking** - Shows order, comparison of values, top/bottom - **●** **Red/Salmon = Part of Whole** - Shows composition, proportions, percentages - **●** **Light Blue = Evolution** - Shows trends, changes over time, trajectories - **●** **Purple = Maps** - Shows geographic/spatial distribution, location-based data - **●** **Pink/Tan = Flow** - Shows movement, transitions, journeys, hierarchies **Tip:** When you see a colored dot next to a chart name, it tells you what analytical goal that chart serves best! --- # Know Your Data ## The 6 Data Type Categories | Data Type | Definition | Examples | |-----------|-----------|----------| | **Numeric** | Continuous measurements | Age, weight, blood pressure, lab values | | **Categoric** | Discrete categories/groups | Gender, disease status, treatment type | | **Ordinal** | Ordered categories | Likert scale, tumor stages, severity levels | | **Time Series** | Temporal/chronological data | Monthly incidence, patient vitals over time | | **Relational** | Connections/networks | Patient pathways, disease networks | | **Map** | Geographic/spatial data | Regional disease rates, location coordinates | --- # The Complete Decision Map ## How Variables Combine ``` SINGLE VARIABLE ├── Numeric → Histogram, Density, Boxplot ├── Categoric → Bar, Pie, Lollipop ├── Ordinal → Ordered Bar, Cumulative Frequency ├── Time Series → Line, Area ├── Map → Choropleth, Bubble Map └── Relational → Network Graph BIVARIATE (TWO VARIABLES) ├── Numeric × Numeric → Scatter, Hexbin, Bubble ├── Numeric × Categoric → Boxplot, Violin, Grouped Bar ├── Categoric × Categoric → Grouped/Stacked Bar, Mosaic, Heatmap ├── Time Series × Numeric → Multi-line, Stacked Area ├── Time Series × Categoric → Faceted Line, Interaction Plot └── Any + Relational → Sankey, Chord MULTIVARIATE (3+ VARIABLES) ├── Numeric × Numeric × Numeric → Bubble, Faceted Scatter ├── Numeric × Multiple Categoric → Faceted Box/Violin, Interaction ├── Multiple Categoric × Multiple Categoric → Sankey, Sunburst, Treemap ├── Time Series × Multiple Variables → Ridgeline, Faceted Line └── Hierarchical → Treemap, Sunburst, Hierarchical Edge Bundling ``` --- # SINGLE VARIABLE: Categoric Data ## ● Distribution | ● Ranking | ● Part of Whole ### Chart Options: - **Bar Chart** ● (counts/frequencies) - **Lollipop Chart** ● (alternative to bar, especially for long lists) - **Cleveland Dot Plot** ● (ranked comparison) - **Pie Chart** ● (≤5 categories only, part-to-whole) - **Doughnut Chart** ● (like pie, better labels) - **Circular Bar Plot** ● (aesthetic alternative) ### Healthcare Examples: - Disease prevalence by state - Hospitalization by insurance type - Comorbidity frequency distribution ### Decision Guide: - **Few categories (<5)** and need part-of-whole → Pie/Doughnut - **Few-moderate categories** → Bar chart (horizontal if long names) - **Many categories (>8)** → Lollipop or Cleveland dot - **Need ranking emphasis** → Ordered bar or lollipop --- # SINGLE VARIABLE: Ordinal Data ## ● Distribution | ● Part of Whole (Ordered) ### Chart Options: - **Ordered Bar Chart** ● (maintain categorical order) - **Ordered Dot Plot** ● - **Cumulative Frequency Plot** ● (especially for Likert scales) - **Frequency Polygon** ● (smooth trend) ### Healthcare Examples: - Patient satisfaction (Likert: 1=Very Unsatisfied to 5=Very Satisfied) - Tumor stages frequency (Stage I → II → III → IV) - Pain severity distribution (None → Mild → Moderate → Severe) - Risk level counts (Low → Medium → High) ### Decision Guide: - **Likert scales** → Stacked ordered bar or cumulative frequency - **Natural progression** (stages, severity) → Maintain order on axis - **Show accumulation** → Cumulative frequency plot - **Compare between groups** → Grouped ordered bar --- # SINGLE VARIABLE: Numeric Data ## ● Distribution ### Chart Options: - **Histogram** ● (shows bin structure, distribution shape) - **Density Plot** ● (smooth, continuous estimate) - **Boxplot** ● (summary: median, quartiles, outliers) - **Violin Plot** ● (distribution + boxplot combined) - **Dot/Strip Plot** ● (individual points, best for small n) ### Healthcare Examples: - Age distribution in cohort - Blood pressure measurements in population - Lab values (HbA1c, cholesterol, creatinine) - Hospital length of stay ### Decision Guide: | Scenario | Best Choice | Why | |----------|------------|-----| | **n < 20** | Dot/Strip plot | See every point | | **n = 20-100** | Histogram + Boxplot | Balance detail & summary | | **n > 100** | Density plot | Smooth, reduces noise | | **Want outliers** | Boxplot | Shows extreme values clearly | | **Want shape details** | Violin plot | Shows multimodality, skewness | --- # SINGLE VARIABLE: Time Series ## ● Evolution ### Chart Options: - **Line Chart** ● (standard for continuous time data) - **Area Chart** ● (emphasizes magnitude/volume) - **Streamgraph** ● (stacked area with flowing theme) ### Healthcare Examples: - Disease incidence trends over years - Hospital admission rates monthly - COVID-19 case counts by week - Patient vital signs during hospitalization ### Decision Guide: - **Single series, continuous time** → Line chart - **Show cumulative volume** → Area chart - **Multiple series, show total** → Stacked area - **Sparse time points** → Line chart with markers --- # SINGLE VARIABLE: Spatial/Map Data ## ● Maps ### Chart Options: - **Choropleth Map** ● (color-coded by region) - **Bubble Map** ● (circles sized by value) - **Heat Map** ● (geographic intensity) - **Dot Map** ● (point locations) ### Healthcare Examples: - Regional disease rates (e.g., TB incidence by state in India) - Hospital bed density by district - Maternal mortality ratios by region - Vaccination coverage by area ### Decision Guide: - **Show rate/percentage by region** → Choropleth - **Show absolute counts by location** → Bubble map - **Show intensity/density** → Heat map - **Specific point locations matter** → Dot map --- # BIVARIATE: Numeric × Numeric ## ● Correlation | ● Distribution ### Chart Options: - **Scatter Plot** ● (relationship between two continuous variables) - **Hexbin Plot** ● (2D histogram for dense data) - **2D Density Plot** ● (contour or heatmap of overlapping points) - **Bubble Plot** ● (3rd variable via size or color) ### Healthcare Examples: - Age vs BMI (body mass relationship) - HbA1c vs Blood Glucose (glycemic control markers) - Creatinine vs eGFR (kidney function) - Systolic vs Diastolic Blood Pressure ### Decision Guide: | Scenario | Best Choice | |----------|------------| | **Moderate sample, clear pattern** | Scatter plot | | **Large n, lots of overplotting** | Hexbin or 2D density | | **Want 3rd variable shown** | Bubble (size) or color gradient | | **Focused region interest** | Zoomed scatter with annotations | --- # BIVARIATE: Numeric Outcome × Categoric Predictor ## ● Distribution | ● Correlation (Comparison) ### Chart Options: - **Boxplot** ● (median, quartiles, outliers by group) - **Violin Plot** ● (distribution shape by group) - **Jittered Dot/Strip/Beeswarm Plot** ● (individual points by group) - **Bar Chart with Error Bars** ● (mean/median ± SD/IQR) - **Cleveland Dot Plot** ● (ranked group means) ### Healthcare Examples: - HbA1c levels across treatment arms - BMI by disease status (healthy vs diabetic vs obese) - Blood pressure by gender - Hospital length of stay by admission type ### Decision Guide: | Sample Size | Distribution Focus | Summary Focus | |-------------|-------------------|---------------| | **n < 30** | Dot/Strip + Boxplot | Not recommended | | **n = 30-100** | Violin or Boxplot | Bar with error bars | | **n > 100** | Violin plot | Density overlay + mean line | | **Outliers matter** | Boxplot + jitter | Always show | | **Group ranking focus** | Ranked dots | Lollipop chart | --- # BIVARIATE: Categoric Outcome × Numeric Predictor ## ● Correlation (Probability) ### Chart Options: - **Logistic Regression Curve** ● (smooth probability line) - **Density Overlay** ● (stacked densities by category) - **Grouped Histogram/Density** ● (overlapping distributions) ### Healthcare Examples: - Disease presence/absence across age ranges - Treatment response (yes/no) by baseline score - Adverse event (yes/no) by medication dose - Mortality (yes/no) by APACHE score ### Visualization: - X-axis: Numeric predictor (age, score, dose) - Y-axis: Probability or proportion - Two groups shown as overlapping curves or stacked --- # BIVARIATE: Categoric × Categoric ## ● Distribution | ● Ranking | ● Part of Whole | ● Correlation ### Chart Options: - **Grouped Bar Chart** ● (side-by-side comparison) - **Dodged Bar Chart** ● (similar to grouped) - **Stacked Bar Chart** ● (shows totals + composition) - **Stacked Bar (Proportional)** ● (percentage/100% stacked) - **Mosaic Plot** ● (area ∝ frequency, shows association) - **Heatmap** ● (color intensity for cell frequencies) ### Healthcare Examples: - Gender vs Disease status (M/F vs HIV+/HIV-) - Treatment arm vs Adverse event (Drug A/B vs AE Yes/No) - Hospital site vs Patient outcome (Site 1-3 vs Recovered/Died) - Risk level by comorbidity count ### Decision Guide: | Goal | Best Chart | |------|-----------| | **Compare totals & subgroups** | Grouped bar | | **Show composition per category** | Stacked bar | | **Show percentages only** | Stacked bar (proportional) | | **Detect association strength** | Mosaic or heatmap | | **Many categories, dense** | Heatmap with color gradient | --- # BIVARIATE: Ordinal × Numeric ## ● Distribution (Ordered) ### Chart Options: - **Ordered Boxplot** ● (boxplot by ordinal groups, maintaining order) - **Ordered Violin Plot** ● (violin by ordinal groups) - **Ordered Jittered Points** ● (points by group, groups ordered) ### Healthcare Examples: - Medication efficacy vs dose level (Low/Medium/High) - Lab value vs disease severity (Stage I-IV) - Pain score vs treatment intensity (Mild/Moderate/Severe) - Functional status vs age group (Young/Middle/Elderly) ### Key Point: - Always maintain explicit ordering on axis - Example: Severity I → II → III → IV (not random order) --- # BIVARIATE: Time Series × Numeric ## ● Evolution | ● Correlation (Trend) ### Chart Options: - **Line Chart** ● (single series over time) - **Multi-line Chart** ● (multiple series overlay) - **Area Chart** ● (cumulative volume over time) - **Stacked Area Chart** ● (composition over time) - **Connected Scatter** ● (if sparse time points) ### Healthcare Examples: - Disease incidence trends over years (single disease) - Patient vital signs over hospital stay (temperature, BP, HR) - Medication effectiveness over weeks (Drug A vs B) - Mortality rates over decades by region ### Decision Guide: - **Single series** → Line chart - **Few series (2-3) to compare** → Multi-line chart - **Many series, want to show total** → Stacked area - **Series showing parts of whole** → Stacked area - **Sparse measurements** → Line with markers or connected scatter --- # BIVARIATE: Time Series × Categoric ## ● Evolution (By Group) | ● Correlation (Group Comparison) ### Chart Options: - **Grouped Line Chart** ● (separate lines for each group) - **Faceted Line Chart** ● (separate subplots per group) - **Grouped Area Chart** ● (stacked or overlapping) - **Interaction Plot** ● (lines intersecting showing interaction) - **Ribbon Chart** ● (flowing bands representing groups) ### Healthcare Examples: - Mortality rate trends (gender comparison: M vs F) - Hospital admission trends by institution (5-year follow-up) - Drug effectiveness over time by treatment arm - Complication rates by age group over study period ### Decision Guide: - **Few groups (2-3)** → Multi-line chart - **Many groups (5+)** → Faceted line plots - **Want to show total + groups** → Stacked area - **Interaction patterns matter** → Interaction plot (lines cross) - **Space constraints** → Faceting better than overlapping --- # BIVARIATE: Ordinal × Categoric ## ● Distribution (Ordered) | ● Part of Whole (Ordered) ### Chart Options: - **Ordered Grouped Bar Chart** ● (bars by category, groups ordered) - **Ordered Stacked Bar** ● (stacked, ordinal categories in order) - **Faceted Ordered Bar** ● (subplots maintaining order) ### Healthcare Examples: - Patient satisfaction (Likert: 1-5) by hospital ward - Pain severity (None/Mild/Moderate/Severe) by treatment type - Risk level (Low/Med/High) by comorbidity count - Functional status by treatment arm ### Key Point: - Maintain ordinal ordering on one axis - Example: Satisfaction scale always: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 --- # MULTIVARIATE: Numeric × Numeric × Numeric ## 3+ Continuous Variables | ● Correlation ### Chart Options: - **Bubble Plot** ● (x, y, size = 3rd; color/opacity = 4th) - **Faceted Scatter** ● (scatter by groups, multiple subplots) - **3D Scatter** (NOT recommended: distorts perception) ### Healthcare Examples: - Age vs BMI (size=cholesterol, color=treatment arm) - HbA1c vs glucose (size=insulin, faceted by gender) - Systolic vs diastolic BP (colored by smoking status) ### Decision Guide: - **3 variables** → Bubble plot (x, y, size) - **4 variables** → Bubble + color - **5+ variables** → Multiple faceted plots (don't try to cram) --- # MULTIVARIATE: Numeric Outcome × Multiple Numeric Predictors ## ● Correlation Matrix ### Chart Options: - **Correlation Matrix** ● (numeric table of coefficients) - **Correlogram** ● (heatmap with color intensity = correlation strength) - **Scatter Plot Matrix** ● (pairwise scatter plots) ### Healthcare Examples: - Lab inter-correlations: glucose, insulin, triglycerides, HDL, LDL - Vital signs correlations: BP, HR, RR, O2 saturation, temperature - Biomarker relationships in cohort study ### Visualization: - Color intensity (warm = positive, cool = negative) - Cell size may represent correlation strength - Diagonal typically = 1.0 (variable with itself) --- # MULTIVARIATE: Numeric Outcome × Multiple Categoric Predictors ## ● Distribution (Faceted) | ● Correlation (Interaction) ### Chart Options: - **Faceted Boxplot/Violin** ● (boxplot per group, subplots for 3rd variable) - **Interaction Plot** ● (lines connecting means by two factors) - **Faceted Scatter + regression lines** ● (by groups) ### Healthcare Examples: - HbA1c by treatment type, faceted by gender (4 subplots: 2 treat × 2 gender) - Lab values by disease status, colored by age group - Drug efficacy by dose level, faceted by patient comorbidity ### Visualization Strategy: - Primary grouping on axis - Secondary grouping via facets or colors - Show interactions: do lines cross? Do patterns differ? --- # MULTIVARIATE: Time Series × Multiple Variables ## ● Evolution (Advanced) | ● Distribution (Temporal) ### Chart Options: - **Multi-line Chart with Faceting** ● (separate subplots per group) - **Ridgeline Plot** ● (distribution by group, stacked vertically) - **Slope Chart** ● (start → end values, multiple series) - **Animated Time Series** ● (interactive exploration) ### Healthcare Examples: - Disease incidence over years, separate lines by region (5 regions) - Patient vitals during admission, faceted by treatment arm - Hospital census by time, colored by department ### Decision Guide: - **Multiple time series + groups** → Faceted multi-line - **Distribution evolution over time** → Ridgeline plot - **Show change from start to end** → Slope chart --- # MULTIVARIATE: Complex Categorical (3+ Categoric) ## ● Flow | ● Part of Whole (Hierarchical) ### Chart Options: - **Sankey Diagram** ● (flow from one category to another) - **Alluvial Diagram** ● (similar to Sankey, broader flows) - **Treemap** ● (nested rectangles for hierarchy) - **Sunburst Chart** ● (nested circles/rings for hierarchy) ### Healthcare Examples: - **Sankey:** Patient flow (admission → diagnostic → treatment → discharge) - **Alluvial:** Disease progression stages (diagnosis → worsening/improvement → outcome) - **Treemap:** Hospital structure (Region → Hospital → Department → Ward) - **Sunburst:** Disease classification (Category → Subcategory → Specific condition) ### Decision Guide: - **Flow/transition/journey** → Sankey or Alluvial - **Nested hierarchy/parts** → Treemap or Sunburst --- # MULTIVARIATE: Relational/Network Data ## ● Flow | ● Correlation (Connections) ### Chart Options: - **Sankey Diagram** ● (directional flows between nodes) - **Chord Diagram** ● (bi-directional relationships, circular) - **Network Graph** ● (nodes + edges, force-directed layout) - **Arc Diagram** ● (nodes in line, arcs show connections) ### Healthcare Examples: - **Sankey:** Patient journeys through clinic system - **Chord:** Disease co-occurrence patterns (patient network) - **Network:** Hospital referral patterns (which hospitals refer to which) - **Arc:** Comorbidity networks (which diseases co-occur) ### Visualization: - Nodes = entities (patients, diseases, hospitals) - Edges/arcs/flows = relationships (referral, co-occurrence) --- # MULTIVARIATE: Hierarchical Data (4+ Levels) ## ● Part of Whole | ● Flow ### Chart Options: - **Treemap** ● (nested rectangles, size ∝ value) - **Sunburst Chart** ● (nested circles, size ∝ value) - **Hierarchical Edge Bundling** ● (connections in hierarchy) ### Healthcare Examples: - **Treemap:** Hospital admissions by Region → State → Hospital → Department (size = admission count) - **Sunburst:** Disease classification by Category → Subcategory → Specific condition → ICD code - **Hierarchical Edge Bundling:** Referral patterns between hospitals at different levels ### Decision Guide: - **Static hierarchy focus** → Treemap - **Want circular aesthetic** → Sunburst - **Complex relationships in hierarchy** → Hierarchical edge bundling --- # SPECIALIZED: Waterfall & Funnel Charts ## ● Flow | ● Part of Whole ### Waterfall Chart - Shows cumulative effect of sequential positive/negative values - **Healthcare Example:** Patient survival from enrollment → screening loss → randomization → completion - Start: 1000 enrolled - Drop: -50 screening failures - Drop: -30 withdrawn consent - End: 920 completed ### Funnel Chart - Stages in a process, showing attrition at each step - **Healthcare Example:** Hospital admission pipeline - Emergency triage: 500 - Admitted: 400 (20% filtered out) - Discharged: 350 (12.5% transferred) - Readmitted: 30 (8.6% recurrent) --- # SPECIALIZED: Advanced Temporal Visualizations ## ● Evolution (Advanced) | ● Distribution (Temporal) ### Streamgraph - Stacked area with flowing, organic theme - **Example:** Emergency admissions over time, stacked by department - Total volume trends visible + department composition ### Calendar Heatmap - Daily/weekly patterns across entire year - **Example:** Hospital occupancy by day of week - Darker = higher occupancy - Pattern reveals peak days/seasons ### Frequency Polygon - Line connecting histogram bins - **Example:** Age distribution comparison between cohorts - Multiple overlaid frequency polygons --- # SPECIALIZED: Text & Network Specialized ## ● Distribution (Text) | ● Correlation (Networks) ### Word Cloud - Text frequency visualization, size = occurrence - **Limitation:** More visual impact than analytic precision - **Healthcare Use:** Patient feedback themes, common symptoms ### Arc Diagram - Network relationships with improved readability over hairball graphs - **Example:** Disease comorbidity network, cleaner than typical network graph ### Hierarchical Edge Bundling - Complex relationship networks with hierarchy - **Example:** Referral patterns between hospitals (different organizational levels) --- # CASE STUDY 1: Real-World Application ## Scenario: "Quarterly revenue by product category over 2 years" ### Step 1: Identify Data Type - **Time component:** Quarterly (Time Series) - **Product component:** Multiple categories (Categoric) - **Revenue component:** Continuous (Numeric) - **Combined:** Time Series + Categoric + Numeric ### Step 2: Define Analytical Goal - **Primary:** ● Evolution (how revenue changes over time) - **Secondary:** ● Correlation (how categories compare) ### Step 3: Chart Options | Option | Chart Type | Pros | Cons | |--------|-----------|------|------| | A | Multi-line chart ● | Clear trend per product | Can be cluttered if >5 products | | B | Stacked area ● | Show total + composition | Hard to compare individual products | | C | Faceted line charts ● | Each product clear | Uses more space | | D | Grouped bar chart ● | Periodic view (snapshot) | Less sense of continuous trend | --- # CASE STUDY 2: Healthcare Example ## Scenario: "HbA1c levels across three treatment arms over 12 months" ### Step 1: Identify Data Type - **Time component:** Baseline, 6mo, 12mo (Time Series - discrete) - **Group component:** 3 treatment arms (Categoric) - **Outcome component:** HbA1c values (Numeric) - **Combined:** Time Series + Categoric + Numeric ### Step 2: Define Analytical Goal - **Primary:** ● Evolution (trajectories over follow-up) - **Secondary:** ● Correlation (do arms differ?) - **Tertiary:** ● Distribution (spread within each arm at each timepoint) ### Step 3: Chart Options | Option | Chart Type | Visualization | |--------|-----------|---------------| | A | Multi-line ± CI ● | One line per arm, shaded confidence bands | | B | Faceted violin plots ● | 3 subplots (one per arm), violin at each timepoint | | C | Spaghetti plot ● | Individual patient trajectories, color-coded by arm | | D | Interaction plot ● | Means connected by lines, x-axis = timepoint | --- # CASE STUDY 3: Multi-Dimensional Complexity ## Scenario: "Top 10 competitors' market share over 5 years by region" ### Step 1: Identify Data Type - **Time:** Years (Time Series) - **Competitors:** 10 categories (Categoric) - **Regions:** Multiple regions (Categoric) - **Market share:** Percentage (Numeric) - **Dimensions:** 4 (too many for single plot!) ### Step 2: Define Analytical Goal - ● Evolution (trends over time) - ● Ranking (who's leading?) - ● Correlation (how do regions differ?) - ● Composition (what % of total?) ### Step 3: Chart Options | Option | Approach | |--------|----------| | **A** | Stacked area per region (faceted: 3-5 subplots) ● ● | | **B** | Grouped multi-line (each region = different color) ● | | **C** | Animated bar chart (top 10 race by region) ● ● | | **D** | Interactive dashboard (toggle region) ● | ### Decision: - **Best static option:** Faceted stacked area (shows time, composition, region comparison) - **Best interactive:** Animated bar or dashboard --- # Common Pitfalls to Avoid ## ❌ What NOT to Do ### ❌ Pie charts with 10+ categories - **Why?** Human perception fails with small angles - **Solution:** Use bar chart ●, lollipop ●, or split into multiple pies ### ❌ 3D charts - **Why?** Perspective distorts data perception (3D cone/pyramid/sphere) - **Solution:** Stick to 2D representations ### ❌ Dual-axis charts - **Why?** Can mislead by manipulating axis scales - **Solution:** Use faceting or separate plots instead ### ❌ Wrong color coding - **Why?** Color should reinforce analytical goal (not random aesthetic) - **Solution:** Sequential colors for magnitude, categorical colors for groups ### ❌ Overplotting (overlapping points) - **Why?** Can't see density or exact position - **Solution:** Use transparency (alpha), jitter, hexbin ●, or density plots ● ### ❌ Stacked bars for detailed comparison - **Why?** Only first and last categories are easy to compare - **Solution:** Use grouped bar ● or faceting for detailed comparison ### ❌ Too many dimensions on one plot - **Why?** Cognitive overload, hard to extract insight - **Solution:** Split into multiple focused visualizations --- # Quick Decision Matrix (Cheat Sheet) ## Analytical Goal × Data Type Reference | Goal \ Data Type | Numeric | Categoric | Ordinal | Time Series | Relational | Map | |------------------|---------|-----------|---------|-------------|-----------|-----| | **Distribution** 🟡 | Hist ●, Density, Box, Violin | Bar ●, Pie | Ordered Bar ● | Line, Area | Network | Choropleth | | **Correlation** 🔵 | Scatter ●, Bubble, Hex | Mosaic ●, Heatmap | Ordered Box ● | Multi-line ● | Sankey, Chord | Choropleth | | **Ranking** 🟢 | Dot ● | Lollipop ●, Bar | Ordered Bar ● | Line (end) | - | - | | **Part of Whole** 🔴 | - | Pie ●, Stacked Bar, Treemap | Stacked (ordered) | Stacked Area ● | Sankey, Treemap | Choropleth | | **Evolution** 🔵 | Line ●, Area | - | - | Line, Area, Ribbon ● | - | Animated Map | | **Maps** 🟣 | - | - | - | - | - | All map types ● | | **Flow** 🟤 | - | - | - | - | Sankey ●, Chord, Network | - | --- # Your Turn: Practice Exercises ## Apply What You've Learned ### Scenario 1: Employee Satisfaction **Question:** Show employee satisfaction scores (Likert 1-5) across hospital departments, comparing before/after intervention - What data types are present? - What analytical goal(s)? - Recommend chart type(s) :::{.notes} Answer: Ordinal × Categoric + Time (before/after) Goals: Distribution (satisfaction spread), Comparison (departments differ?), Evolution (did intervention help?) Charts: Faceted ordered bar / Grouped stacked bar / Interaction plot ::: --- # Your Turn: Practice Exercises (continued) ### Scenario 2: Website Analytics **Question:** Display website traffic sources (organic, paid, direct, referral) and their conversion rates over 6 months - What data types are present? - What analytical goal(s)? - Recommend chart type(s) :::{.notes} Answer: Categoric (traffic source) × Numeric (conversion %) + Time (monthly) Goals: Evolution (trends), Comparison (which source converts best?), Part-of-whole (traffic distribution) Charts: Multi-line chart / Stacked area / Faceted line per source ::: --- # Your Turn: Practice Exercises (continued) ### Scenario 3: Clinical Trial Recruitment **Question:** Track patient recruitment rates by site and treatment arm monthly through a 2-year trial - What data types are present? - What analytical goal(s)? - Recommend chart type(s) :::{.notes} Answer: Time (monthly) × Categoric (sites, arms) + Numeric (count) Goals: Evolution (enrollment pace), Comparison (which site fastest?), Composition (proportional enrollment) Charts: Multi-line faceted / Grouped bar per month / Stacked area / Interaction plot ::: --- # Your Turn: Practice Exercises (continued) ### Scenario 4: Healthcare - Adverse Events **Question:** Compare adverse event frequencies between two drug treatments across age groups (pediatric, adult, elderly) - What data types are present? - What analytical goal(s)? - Recommend chart type(s) :::{.notes} Answer: Categoric (drug, AE type) × Categoric (age group) + Numeric (count) Goals: Ranking (most common AEs), Comparison (which drug safer?), Distribution (event frequency) Charts: Grouped bar / Faceted bar / Mosaic / Heatmap ::: --- # Tools & Resources ## Recommended Frameworks & References ### Visualization Tools - **R:** ggplot2, plotly, ggvis - **Python:** matplotlib, seaborn, plotly, altair - **BI Platforms:** Tableau, PowerBI, Looker - **Static/Interactive:** D3.js, Observable ### Reference Resources - **data-to-viz.com** - Yan Holtz's comprehensive decision tree - **R Graph Gallery** (r-graph-gallery.com) - 200+ ggplot2 examples - **ggplot2 documentation** - Official reference + cheat sheets - **Fundamentals of Data Visualization** (Claus Wilke) - Free online book ### Practice Datasets - **UCI Machine Learning Repository** - **Kaggle Datasets** - Thousands of public datasets - **NFHS-V Data** (National Family Health Survey, India) - **GitHub public repositories** - Data visualization examples --- # Key Takeaways ## Core Principles for Effective Visualization ✅ **Always start with your analytical goal** - What question are you answering? (distribute, compare, rank, relate, etc.) ✅ **Data types narrow your options significantly** - Numeric vs Categoric vs Ordinal vs Temporal vs Spatial ✅ **Multiple valid charts may exist—choose based on audience & context** - Scientist ≠ Executive ≠ Patient communication ✅ **Use color strategically to support your analytical goal** - Sequential for magnitude, categorical for groups, diverging for contrasts ✅ **Simplicity trumps complexity; avoid unnecessary dimensions** - If 3D doesn't add insight, keep it 2D - If faceting helps clarity, use it ✅ **When in doubt, check data-to-viz.com or reference examples** - Don't reinvent the wheel; learn from established best practices ✅ **Practice makes perfect—iterate on visualizations** - First draft rarely optimal; refine based on feedback --- # Q&A / Thank You ## Resources & Next Steps ### Key Links - **data-to-viz.com** - Decision tree flowchart - **R Graph Gallery** - Live examples with code - **ggplot2 cheat sheet** - Quick reference ### Questions? - What visualization challenges are YOU facing? - What data type combinations are most common in your work? ### Next Steps - Apply the 3-step framework to your own data - Practice with the scenario exercises - Refer back to the decision matrix when choosing charts --- ## 🔧 Practise in R {.smaller} Download the lab **[Explore by picture](../labs/moderate/m3_explore_plots.R)** and the data ([ncd_survey.csv](../data/ncd_survey.csv)). <script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
